# Intake Brief: Configured test gate excludes the herdr package suite (no herdr test type/group) (WL-0MVGJ4WSS005BMSI)

## Headline

Add a sanctioned `herdr` test type (`run_tests.py --type herdr`) and a `herdr` named group (`--group herdr`) mapped to `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`, so the herdr package suite (107 files / ~3,500 tests) runs through the test skill's runner and cache instead of ad-hoc vitest invocations — while **keeping herdr out of the canonical full gate**, honouring the prior producer decision on WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8.

## Problem statement

`.pi/test-config.json` declares the full suite as `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` + `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`. The `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` suite is therefore never run by any gate, and `run_tests.py --type herdr` fails with an unknown-type error because no local type/group defines it. Child sessions work around this with ad-hoc `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src` runs, which bypass the test skill's sanctioned runner and cache — so the audit cannot see the evidence and a red herdr tree can be pushed to `dev` undetected (WL-0MVFRALLB0065UIW was caught only by a direct vitest run).

## Users

- **Herdr work-item developers** (e.g. WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS AC6/AC8) — need a sanctioned, cache-recording way to run the herdr suite.
  - *User story:* As a herdr work-item developer, when I need to verify herdr changes, I want `run_tests.py --type herdr` to run the package suite and record a cache entry, so the audit can see my evidence without me invoking vitest ad hoc.
- **Producer / reviewer** — wants gate behaviour documented and evidence visible.
  - *User story:* As a producer, I want the documentation to state which suites the dev-push gate runs and how to run the herdr suite, so gate expectations are no longer ambiguous.
- **Implement skill** — wants changed-scope selection to pick the herdr suite for herdr-touching items.
  - *User story:* As the implement skill, when changed files are under `packages/herdr/`, I want the changed-scope gate to map to the `herdr` group, so finish-time validation targets exactly the affected suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `python3 run_tests.py --type herdr --json` (default scope `full`) resolves to `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`, executes it, and records a cache entry under the `herdr` type key — a repeat invocation within the 2h TTL is served from cache (`cached: true`) and never satisfies the audit's full-suite query (only `--type full` scope `full` entries do).
- AC2: `python3 run_tests.py --group herdr --json` also works via a `groups.herdr` entry in `.pi/test-config.json`, and the group's `paths: ["packages/herdr/**"]` makes implement.py's changed-scope gate auto-select the herdr group when a change touches `packages/herdr/` (SA-0MUJKF2HP001BR51). Both type and group land in this item per D2.
- AC3: The canonical full suite is **unchanged** — `run_tests.py --type full` still runs exactly `tests/cli` + `tests/unit`; herdr is **not** added to `suiteCommands` (producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 preserved and documented).
- AC4: Extension contract held: `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` defines `types.herdr`; minimum types it omits (`unit`/`smoke`) fail with the runner's loud diagnostic (never a silent full-suite substitution), and `--type full` still works via the suiteCommands fallback.
- AC5 (validation): A verification step proves AC1–AC4: run `--type herdr` twice (first cold, second cached), `--group herdr`, `--type full` unchanged, and `--type unit`/`--type smoke` produce the expected loud diagnostics.
- AC6 (docs): The dev-gate documentation (`docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`, new **Test gates** section, cross-linked from `packages/herdr/README.md` "Run tests") states which suites the dev-push gate runs and how to run the herdr suite (`--type herdr` / `--group herdr`), and records the producer decision that herdr stays out of the full gate.
- AC7 (docs): All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes — code comments, `.pi/test-config.json`/extension file comments, README and any relevant wiki/docs entries. (CHANGELOG.md excluded.)
- AC8 (full suite): The full project test suite passes with the new changes (canonical gate green and untouched).

## Constraints

- **Producer decision (hard constraint):** herdr tests must **not** join the canonical full suite — WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 closed Won't fix: "the herdr tests will not be run as part of the canonical full suite". Cost of adding ~12–19 min per gate (item estimate) and observed flaky/order-dependent failures in 2026-10-20 runs justify a separate, opt-in gate.
- **Extension contract:** a local extension with a `types` map that omits a minimum type (`unit`/`smoke`) makes that type fail loudly (never silent full-suite substitution, AC4). Today `--type unit` already fails via convention (no pytest/`.mjs` in `tests/unit`), so the extension introduces no functional regression — the diagnostic text changes, which must be verified.
- **Suite command:** `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src` (vitest path filter) — the command verified in WL-0MVFE1IRB0004X1U.
- **Audit evidence scope:** `herdr`-type and `group:herdr` cache entries are **not** audit-accepted full-suite evidence (SA-0MT6BYQHB008DOGC). Audits of herdr-only items still require operator attestation (`--green-run HEAD`) or extended audit support (out of scope here — follow-up opportunity).
- **Runtime estimate discrepancy:** the work item says ~12–19 min; WL-0MVFE1IRB0004X1U measured ~130 s standalone (107 files / 3,510 tests, idle host). Re-measure at implementation start and record the figure in the doc update.

## Existing state

- `.pi/test-config.json`: `suiteCommands` = `tests/cli` + `tests/unit`; no `groups` key.
- No `.pi/skills_extensions/test/` directory; `run_tests.py --type herdr` → "Unknown test type 'herdr'" error.
- Repo `.githooks/pre-push` runs branch policy + context budget + `wl sync` only — it does **not** run the test suite (the framework's test-gated pre-push is not installed here); the test gate runs via `implement.py finish` changed-scope and the `ship` release gate, both reading `full_suite_commands`.

## Desired change

1. Create `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` with `{"types": {"herdr": ["npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src"]}}`.
2. Add `"groups": {"herdr": {"commands": ["npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src"], "paths": ["packages/herdr/**"]}}` to `.pi/test-config.json` (keeps `suiteCommands` untouched).
3. Document the gates and the herdr invocation in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (new **Test gates** section) and cross-link from `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` — NEW: `types.herdr` type map (`npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`).
- `.pi/test-config.json` — ADD `groups.herdr` (commands + `paths: ["packages/herdr/**"]`); leave `suiteCommands` unchanged.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — ADD "Test gates" section: suites the dev-push gate runs, how to run herdr, producer decision on the full gate.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — ADD "Run the suite via the sanctioned runner" note (`run_tests.py --type herdr` / `--group herdr`).
- Tests: no new source tests required for JSON config; verification is command-level (AC5). If the repo's test conventions require unit tests for config, add minimal ones under `tests/`.

## Related work

- WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 (completed, Won't fix) — same underlying problem (herdr excluded from canonical suite); producer decided herdr does **not** join the full gate. This item fills the remaining gap: sanctioned type/group + docs, without overturning that decision.
- WL-0MVFE1IRB0004X1U (completed) — full herdr suite verification (107 files / 3,510 tests, ~130 s standalone); confirms the exact suite command.
- WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS (open, plan_complete) — herdr audit-dispatch feature whose AC6/AC8 require the herdr suite; immediate beneficiary.
- WL-0MVFRALLB0065UIW (completed test-failure) — herdr regression found only via ad-hoc vitest; evidence of the gap.
- WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR (open, intake_complete) — sibling item: *Canonical test suite excludes 76 root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files*; same gap family, different excluded set (`tests/*` root files vs `packages/herdr/src`). Complementary, not overlapping; both may touch the same doc target below.
- Framework test-skill docs (`skill/test/docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`, `skill-extensions.md` in the framework repo) — type-map and groups contract; SA-0MUJKF2HP001BR51, SA-0MTJQB2MA008HMO6.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Decision (documented, not blocking):** herdr stays a **separate gate** (type/group), not part of the full `suiteCommands` — honours the explicit producer decision on WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8. Producer may override; recorded in the Appendix.
- **Changed-scope interaction:** adding `groups.herdr` changes implement.py finish behaviour for herdr-touching items — finish runs only the herdr group, not the canonical changed-scope subset (which is deferred to the dev-push gate). This is the intended "gate invoked by items that touch it"; the canonical suite is still enforced by the dev-push/ship gates for repos with the framework pre-push installed. Mitigation: AC6 documents this and the repo's pre-push currently does **not** run the suite at all — a pre-existing gap worth a follow-up item (scope-creep guard: do not fix it here).
- **Current tree state:** an environment run at 2026-10-20 18:10 observed 3 failures + 2 unhandled errors in `worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts` and `worklist-blocked-by-cache.test.ts` (timing/order-sensitive, Green-circle and Blocked By rendering) — treat the herdr suite as potentially red at this moment; re-verify before relying on `--type herdr` evidence during implementation.
- **Runtime discrepancy (~130 s vs 12–19 min):** re-measure; record ground truth in the docs.
- **Audit evidence gap:** herdr-type entries aren't full-suite evidence; follow-up: teach the audit/`query_cached` to consult the `herdr` group entry for herdr-touching items (record as `discovered-from:WL-0MVGJ4WSS005BMSI`, do NOT do it in this item).
- **Scope creep guard:** `tests/herdr/` (20 files), `tests/bench`, `tests/integration`, etc. remain outside this item — only `packages/herdr/src` per the seed intent; further suite-extensions become follow-up items.
- **Shared doc target with sibling:** WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR also plans a docs/dev/ test-suite-layout update — coordinate the **Test gates** section (AC6) so the two land without conflicting edits (same file `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` is the likely target).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & decisions

- D1 (decision, from producer record, not a live question): *Should the herdr suite join the canonical full gate?* — **Answer (producer, via WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 closure):** No — "the herdr tests will not be run as part of the canonical full suite — the producer does not want to run the herdr tests." This brief implements the gap the closure left open (sanctioned opt-in type/group + documentation). Research: closure comment on WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 (2026-10-20); suite runtime + flakiness evidence recorded in its intake comment and in WL-0MVFE1IRB0004X1U.
- D2 (assumption, overridable): the named `groups.herdr` (changed-scope auto-selection) is in scope alongside the `types.herdr` map, per the seed intent "Add a herdr test type/group". If the producer prefers type-only, AC2 is dropped and implement.py changed-scope selection is left as-is.

## Related work (find-related automated report)

Automated scan (`find_related.py`, WL-0MVGJ4WSS005BMSI) cross-references:

- **WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR** (open, intake_complete) — *Canonical test suite excludes 76 root-level `tests/*.test.ts` files*: sibling item in the same gap family (different excluded set: root `tests/*` files). Complementary; also references a shared future **Test gates** doc section.
- **WL-0MQDR51JO0037ISJ** (completed) — *Eliminate unsafe as-casts in shortcut dispatch*: tangential, no overlap — excluded-set unrelated; noted for traceability only.
- **WL-0MQOIBGIR006CWLR** (completed) — *Add Background Task Runtime for Non-Blocking Operations*: tangential, no overlap — noted for traceability only.

Repository matches: `packages/herdr/README.md` (already a Key File), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (dispatcher docs, not a gate doc — no change needed), `CLI.md` (CLI docs, no change needed).

## Problem (measured by F10 — WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J)

A herdr refresh tick runs **five** separate `wl` spawns per pane (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`): the four mandatory `wl list` subsets plus the `wl next` browse feed. Measured on the reference host with 4 panes over a 30 s cycle (20 items, 5 s refresh):

| | pre-F4 CLI | after F4–F7 | target |
|---|---|---|---|
| spawns / cycle | 120 | 120 | — |
| CPU-seconds / cycle | 159.44 | **83.58** | **63.78** (0.4× baseline) |
| CPU-s per spawn | 1.329 | **0.697** | ≤ 0.53 |
| peak RSS | 78.8 MB | 68 MB | — |

The F4–F7 fast path achieved a **47.6 %** CPU-second reduction (short of the 60 % target). The dominant remaining cost is **per-spawn Node startup**, not `wl` work: the bare-node floor is ~0.46 CPU-s of the 0.70 CPU-s per spawn (~66 %). Even a zero-cost `wl` body would cap the reduction at ~65 %, so faster spawns cannot reach 60 % with five spawns per tick — **fewer spawns** is the lever.

## Goal

One `wl` read per pane per refresh tick instead of five, with identical refresh output.

## Acceptance criteria

- A single `wl` invocation returns every subset the worklist needs (critical, in_review review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots, browse feed) — e.g. a `--worklist-bundle` mode or a dedicated `wl worklist --json` command — sharing one DB open and one cache entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` issues that single read per refresh tick; the mandatory-subset guarantees (critical always shown, blocked always shown, review queue always shown) are preserved by tests.
- Measured with `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10): total CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle with 4 panes drops to ≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline (≤ 63.8 CPU-s), ideally ~5× fewer spawns.
- Cache correctness unchanged: identical JSON for identical DB state, write invalidation still bumps the state counter, worktree/`--worklog-dir` behaviour unchanged.
- herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state (existing fetcher tests + spawn-reduction simulation pass).

## Evidence / how to reproduce

```sh
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh -- --json --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5
```

Discovered from F10 (WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J), which recorded the shortfall and identified spawn count as the remaining lever.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J** – Verify >=60% CPU-second reduction per refresh cycle (completed)
- **WL-0MSHJ2NWZ000P3X9** – [test-failure] read-cache spawn reduction (6-pane simulation) cuts work spawns by ≥60% across a simulated 6-pane refresh — failing test (completed)
- **WL-0MVFRR98A008MM19** – Spawn instrumentation: per-process CPU and RSS (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, always, bare, baseline, behaviour (+101 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: always, bare, baseline, behaviour, bench (+92 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: achieved, always, bare, behaviour, blocked (+86 more)

# Verify herdr test type and group gate

**Parent:** WL-0MVGJ4WSS005BMSI — Configured test gate excludes the herdr package suite (no herdr test type/group)

## Summary

Test-first verification slice: prove the sanctioned `herdr` test type and named group behave exactly as the parent specifies (parent AC1–AC8), using the test skill's runner (`run_tests.py`) so every run is cache-recorded. Runs after the config child lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `python3 run_tests.py --type herdr --json` (default scope `full`) resolves to `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`, executes it, and records a cache entry under the `herdr` type key — a repeat invocation within the 2h TTL is served from cache (`cached: true`).
- AC2: `python3 run_tests.py --group herdr --json` also works via a `groups.herdr` entry in `.pi/test-config.json`, and the group's `paths` make implement.py's changed-scope gate auto-select the herdr group when a change touches `packages/herdr/`.
- AC3: `python3 run_tests.py --type full --json` still runs exactly `tests/cli` + `tests/unit`; herdr is **not** included in the canonical full suite.
- AC4: `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` defines `types.herdr`; minimum types it omits (`unit`/`smoke`) fail with the runner's loud diagnostic (never a silent full-suite substitution), and `--type full` still works via the suiteCommands fallback.
- AC5: A verification step proves AC1–AC4: run `--type herdr` twice (first cold, second cached), `--group herdr`, `--type full` unchanged, and `--type unit`/`--type smoke` produce the expected loud diagnostics.
- AC6: The full project test suite passes with the new changes (canonical gate green and untouched).

## Minimal Implementation

- Run the AC1–AC4 command matrix and capture the JSON results (cold run, cached re-run, group run, full run, unit/smoke diagnostics); confirm AC6 (full suite green) at the end.
- Triage genuine failures into critical `test-failure` items via the triage helper; do not fix herdr flakiness inside this item.
- Re-measure the herdr suite runtime (`time npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`) and post the figure for the docs child.
- No source or config changes in this child — verification evidence only.

## Dependencies

- Depends on: "Add herdr test type and named group" (config child) — the type/group cannot be verified before they exist.
- Test-first ordering: created before the implementation child; the dependency edge makes it execute after.

## Deliverables

- Comment on the parent with the AC matrix results and measured herdr runtime.
- Triage work items for any genuine failures found.
